title: Conseil d’État to rule on school-attire décret in laïcité dispute
content: The Conseil d’État will rule next month on the legality of the school-attire *décret* adopted in August, after a parents’ collectif challenged it through a *référé*, arguing that the text exceeds the laïcité principles set out in the education loi of 2019.

The décret extends the existing prohibition on conspicuous religious symbols to municipal extracurricular activities financed by the member republics, and requires recteurs to publish annual reports on its application. The collectif argues that the extension covers activities outside the scope defined by the legislature.

During the hearing on Tuesday, the rapporteur public recommended rejecting the référé, while observing that the boundary between school time and municipal activities “deserves clarification from the legislature rather than administrative practice”. That formulation has been read by both sides as an invitation and a warning.

The three eastern republics have already issued implementing guidance, and the académies have circulated instructions to school directors. In Aurelle, several municipalities have suspended the financing of after-school programmes pending the ruling, a decision that parents’ associations describe as a premature application of a contested text.

“Laïcité is not a neutral instrument, but a guarantee that no child is treated differently because of a conviction; the décret protects that guarantee,” said the president of République et École, a citizens’ association that intervened in support of the government. The collectif’s spokeswoman replied that “protecting a principle does not authorise extending it by administrative decree”.

The case illustrates a broader tension: the Conseil constitutionnel upheld the 2019 laïcité loi in full, but its reasoning repeatedly referred to the school as the space in which the rule applies. Extending the same rule to municipal premises raises a question the court has not yet addressed.

A ruling is expected in the first half of November. Whatever the outcome, school directors in the affected republics will begin the winter term without a settled answer to the most practical question of all: which activities fall inside the rule, and who decides.
author: Texte : Margot Delaunay — Agence des Républiques (ADR) · Photographies : Lucie Sorbier — Presses de Vallonne
